Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Stinging/burning pain with urination for a few days; mild lower abdominal (suprapubic) crampy pain with voiding.
  - No clear trigger/exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset a few days ago; persistent but not severe.
  - One episode of small amount of blood in urine earlier today; urine described as malodorous.
  - Denies increased urinary frequency/urgency, flank/back pain, nausea/vomiting, fever, diarrhea.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - No ENT or airway symptoms reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - No prior similar episodes documented.
  - Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate without relief.
  - No prior ED visits/hospitalization reported.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as “not documented”).
  - Allergy: Clindamycin → “swelling” (distribution/severity/timing not documented).
  - Regular meds: None.
  - New prescription: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact agent, dose/strength, and route not documented).
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Sexually active with boyfriend of ~2 months; uses condoms; no vaginal discharge.
  - LMP ~3 weeks ago; pregnancy thought unlikely; has never had an STI screen.
  - Lives with roommates near college; student; drinks alcohol socially; non-smoker.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - None observed/reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - No respiratory complaints; no stridor/noisy breathing reported.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - No dizziness/syncope reported; alert and interactive.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise write “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower UTI).
- Evidence: Short history of dysuria and suprapubic crampy pain, brief gross hematuria, malodorous urine; denies fever, flank/back pain, nausea/vomiting—supports lower tract infection; otherwise healthy 19-year-old.
- DDx (aligned with transcript):
  1) Acute uncomplicated cystitis – most likely given dysuria, suprapubic discomfort, hematuria, malodor; opposing: absence of frequency/urgency (not mandatory).
  2) Urethritis due to STI (Chlamydia/Gonorrhea/Mycoplasma) – possible with new partner and no prior screening; opposing: no discharge or pelvic symptoms.
  3) Vaginitis (BV/Trichomonas) causing external dysuria – malodor could be vaginal; opposing: no discharge/pruritus; hematuria favors urinary source.
- No acute ENT pathology identified. Medication allergy noted (clindamycin-associated swelling).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact agent/dose/route not documented).
  - Increase oral fluids; cranberry juice permitted.
  - Avoid sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception thereafter.
- Specific patient/caregiver instructions:
  - If symptoms are not improved by end of the week, return/call for reassessment.
  - Avoid clindamycin due to prior swelling.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Seek prompt care if fever develops, back/flank pain occurs, worsening systemic symptoms, gross hematuria persists/worsens, or if new pelvic pain/abnormal discharge occurs.
  - If any swelling of lips/tongue/face, throat tightness, voice change, trouble breathing, or rash after starting antibiotics, stop medication and seek emergency care immediately.
- Follow-up:
  - If persistent or recurrent symptoms: consider urinalysis/urine culture and STI screening (Chlamydia/Gonorrhea/Mycoplasma); consider pelvic exam if vaginal symptoms arise.
  - Pregnancy test if any concern regarding possible pregnancy.
  - No current indication for ENT/allergy referral; consider allergy evaluation in future if antibiotic-associated swelling suggests prior angioedema (details not documented).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Detailed characterization of clindamycin allergy (timing, distribution of swelling, severity, airway involvement), full allergy list, prior anaphylaxis history, availability of epinephrine auto-injector.
  - Vitals and physical exam not recorded.
  - Urinalysis/urine culture not obtained; pregnancy test not performed.
  - STI screening not performed; prior UTI history not documented.
  - Exact antibiotic agent, dose/strength, and route not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor audio interruptions/clarifications but adequate for clinical documentation.
